mainTopic: Damage caused while acting with permission: beam and barrel on the road, a husband and wife, cows in the street, and runners in the public domain.
overview: The משנה finishes its rules about two people walking on a public road, one carrying a beam (קורה) and one carrying a barrel (חבית), and it applies the same rules to a lamp (נר) and flax (פשתן). The גמרא asks whether a husband who injures his wife during תשמיש המטה is exempt because he acted with permission. רב הונא says he is exempt, based on the משנה's 'permission to walk.' רבא argues with a קל וחומר from the forest case that the husband is liable, because he alone performs the action. Next, ריש לקיש rules about a lying cow and a walking cow that kick each other. The גמרא tries to prove his ruling from both parts of the משנה, and each proof is pushed away. A new משנה exempts two people who collide while walking or running. The גמרא shows that this משנה can fit איסי בן יהודה, who makes a runner liable except on ערב שבת at twilight. It then begins to explain why running at that time counts as 'with permission,' using רבי חנינא's practice, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Beam carrier in front stops suddenly
steps.stepSummary: When the beam carrier walks first and suddenly stops, he is liable for the broken barrel. If he warned the barrel carrier to stop, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beam owner (walking in front) stopped, he is liable. If he told the barrel owner 'Stop!', he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case where the בעל קורה walks in front and the בעל חבית walks behind. It explains what happens if the man in front stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the one in front is not liable, because the one behind should watch where he walks. But if the one in front stops suddenly, the one behind could not expect it, so the one in front pays. If he warned 'Stop!', the one behind should have listened, so the one in front is exempt again.

keyTerms.meaning: The person carrying a wooden beam

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of the case. The case (beam in front, barrel behind) begins in the משנה on the previous עמוד, so 'he' who stopped is the one walking in front.

phrases.english: And if the owner of the beam stopped, he is liable.
And if he said to the owner of the barrel, 'Stop!', he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous עמוד (beam first, barrel behind).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A front walker who stops suddenly is liable. A front walker who warned the one behind first is exempt.

steps.title: Barrel carrier in front, beam carrier behind
steps.stepSummary: Now the order is reversed. The beam carrier behind is liable if the barrel breaks. He is exempt if the barrel carrier stopped suddenly, but liable again if the barrel carrier warned him to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the barrel owner was first and the beam owner last, and the barrel broke on the beam, the beam owner is liable. If the barrel owner stopped, the beam owner is exempt. If the barrel owner told the beam owner 'Stop!', the beam owner is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the order: the barrel carrier walks in front and the beam carrier behind. It goes through the same three situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one walking behind is expected to watch out, so the beam carrier pays. A sudden stop by the one in front is not his fault, so he is exempt. If he was warned to stop and did not, he is liable again.
steps.whatToRemember: The one behind must be careful. The one in front pays only if he stopped suddenly without warning. A warning moves the responsibility onto the one who was warned.

phrases.english: If the owner of the barrel was first
and the owner of the beam was last,
and the barrel was broken by the beam, he is liable.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the beam carrier, the one walking behind.

phrases.english: And if the owner of the barrel stopped, he is exempt.
And if he said to the owner of the beam, 'Stop!', he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה בַּעַל חָבִית רִאשׁוֹן וּבַעַל קוֹרָה אַחֲרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 1, with the order of walkers reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beam carrier behind is liable. He is exempt if the barrel carrier stopped suddenly, and liable if he was warned to stop.

steps.title: Same rules for a lamp and flax
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the same rules apply when one person carries a lamp and the other carries flax that catches fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true when one comes with his lamp and the other with his flax.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends everything it just said to a new case: a נר and פשתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a beam breaking a barrel, now a lamp sets flax on fire. Who pays is decided the same way: who was in front, who stopped, and who warned.

phrases.english: And similarly, if this one comes with his lamp
and that one with his flax.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן זֶה בָּא בְּנֵרוֹ וְזֶה בְּפִשְׁתָּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rules of steps 1–2 to a parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rules for beam and barrel apply equally to lamp and flax.

steps.title: Is a husband liable for injuring his wife during relations?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר נתן asks רב הונא about a husband who injures his wife during תשמיש המטה. Is he exempt because the act is permitted, or should he have been careful?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר נתן asked רב הונא: if someone injures his wife during marital relations, what is the law? Since he is acting with permission, is he exempt? Or perhaps he should have paid attention?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. It sets up two sides and waits for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the husband is doing something he is allowed to do, so maybe he is not responsible for harm. Side two: even when allowed, he must still be careful, so maybe he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
He should have paid attention, been careful

steps.whyThisMatters: This asks a general question. Does doing something you are allowed to do free you from paying for harm you cause along the way?

phrases.english: Gemara

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר נָתָן מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Natan asked Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּזִּיק אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּתַשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: One who injures his wife during marital relations, what is the law?
Since he is acting with permission, is he exempt,
or perhaps he should have paid attention?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר נָתָן מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a new question tied to the idea of acting with permission.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether acting בִּרְשׁוּת exempts a husband from damages for injuring his wife, or whether he must still be careful.

steps.title: רב הונא answers from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the answer is already in the משנה, which exempts because 'this one has permission to walk and that one has permission to walk.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it in the משנה: 'For this one has permission to walk, and that one has permission to walk.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. He points to a line in the משנה about the beam and barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempted the beam carrier because both people were allowed to use the road. רב הונא reads this as a rule: acting with permission makes you exempt. So the husband, who is also acting with permission, is exempt too.

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
For this one has permission to walk,
and that one has permission to walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by citing the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Acting with permission brings exemption, as the משנה shows. So the husband is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's reason 'שֶׁלָּזֶה רְשׁוּת לְהַלֵּךְ וְלָזֶה רְשׁוּת לְהַלֵּךְ'.

steps.title: רבא's argument from the forest case
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the husband is liable, using a קל וחומר from someone who accidentally kills while chopping wood in a forest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is a קל וחומר. In a forest, each person enters a place where he has every right to be. Still, the one who kills is treated as if he entered his friend's domain, and he is liable. So this husband, who really does enter someone else's domain, should surely be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רב הונא. He says the husband is liable, and he proves it with a קל וחומר from the forest case in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the forest, both people have equal rights to be there, yet the accidental killer still goes to גלות. The husband is in a weaker position, because he is entering someone else's 'domain' (his wife's body). If the woodcutter is liable even with equal rights, the husband must be liable all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one: if the rule applies there, it surely applies here
Forest, referring to the case in דברים 19:5 of a man who accidentally kills while chopping wood
His own domain, a place where he has a right to be
His friend's domain, someone else's space

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main debate. רב הונא says permission exempts, and רבא says that permission does not protect someone who causes harm.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is an a fortiori inference.
And just as a forest,
phrases.notes: This points to דברים 19:5, where a man chopping wood accidentally kills his friend with a flying axe-head.

phrases.english: where this one enters his own domain
and that one enters his own domain,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס לִרְשׁוּת חֲבֵירוֹ – וְחַיָּיב;
phrases.english: he is treated like one who entered his friend's domain, and he is liable;
phrases.notes: In this case 'liable' means he has to go to an עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: this one, who enters his friend's domain,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes רב הונא's answer in step 5 and offers a different ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband is liable for injuring his wife, by קל וחומר from the forest killer who is liable even when both people have equal rights.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's 'permission to walk'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה exempts because both people had permission to walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches that this one has permission to walk and that one has permission to walk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא by bringing back the same משנה that רב הונא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts damage done by someone acting with permission. That seems to support רב הונא and to contradict רבא's claim that permission does not exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (refers to what the משנה says)
Permission to walk, the right to be in that place

phrases.english: But this teaches
that this one has permission to walk
and that one has permission to walk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling from step 6 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the husband is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts someone acting with permission, and the husband also acts with permission, so he should be exempt.

steps.title: Both walkers act equally, but here only he acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the משנה both people were doing the same thing, but here only the husband is doing the action.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, both of them are the same. Here, he is the one doing the action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that the משנה's case is different from the husband's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, both people were walking, so neither one is more responsible than the other. In תשמיש, the husband is treated as the only active party. Because he alone does the action, his permission does not protect him from liability.

keyTerms.meaning: He is doing an action, he is the active one

phrases.english: There, both of them are alike;
here, he is the one performing an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by distinguishing the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (equal actors vs. a single active actor)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'permission to walk' exempts anyone who acts with permission, including the husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permission exempts only when both sides are equally active. The husband alone acts, so he is liable.

steps.title: Isn't the woman also doing the act?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a פסוק calls both the man and the woman 'the souls that do', so she is also active.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she does not act?! But it is written: 'The souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 8. It brings a פסוק that treats the woman as an active participant too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 8 depended on the husband being the only one who acts. The פסוק about forbidden relations uses the plural 'souls that do', which includes the woman. If she also acts, the two cases are alike again, just like the walkers in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written (introduces a פסוק used as a challenge)
The souls that do them, the people who commit the act

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The גמרא is only questioning step 8's claim that the husband alone acts, and the sugya continues after this.

phrases.english: And she does not?!
But isn't it written:
"And the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29. The word 'souls' is plural, so the woman is counted as one of the people doing the act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's claim that only the husband performs an action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls both partners 'the souls that do', so the woman is also active. That makes the case equal, like the משנה, and the husband should be exempt.

steps.title: Both have pleasure, but only he does the action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the פסוק calls the woman a 'doer' because she also has pleasure. In the injury case, though, only the husband performs the action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pleasure belongs to both of them, but he is the one who is actually doing the action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9 and saves רבא's ruling that the husband is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls both people 'doers' only because both share in the הנאה (pleasure), and that counts as taking part in the sin. When it comes to causing damage, the physical action is his alone. So he is like the person chopping wood in רבא's קל וחומר, and he is חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: Sharing in the pleasure can make someone part of a sin, but liability for damage goes to the person who actually does the physical action.

phrases.english: Pleasure: both of them have it;
but he is the one doing the action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: shared pleasure is not the same as shared action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show that the woman is an active participant, just like the man.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is called active only because of the pleasure. In the injury case, the man alone does the act, so he is חייב.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's rule about a lying cow and a walking cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה of the beam carrier. ריש לקיש rules that a walking cow that kicks a lying cow is exempt, but a lying cow that kicks a walking cow is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the beam carrier was first...' ריש לקיש said: Two cows are in the street, one lying down and one walking. If the walking cow kicked the lying one, its owner is exempt. If the lying cow kicked the walking one, its owner is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה, and brings a ruling from ריש לקיש about cows in the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking in the street is allowed, but lying down in the street is not. So a lying cow that hurts a walking cow puts the blame on the lying cow's owner. A walking cow that hurts a lying cow is exempt, because the lying cow was not supposed to be there.

keyTerms.meaning: The public street, which everyone is allowed to use

steps.confusionAlert: Pay attention to who kicked whom. Liability depends on which cow did the kicking, not only on which cow was lying down.

phrases.english: 'If the owner of the beam was first,' etc.
Reish Lakish said:
Two cows in the public domain,
one lying down and one walking;
if the walking one kicked the lying one, it is exempt.
If the lying one kicked the walking one, it is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the walking cow kicks the lying cow, its owner is פטור. If the lying cow kicks the walking cow, its owner is חייב.

steps.title: Trying to support ריש לקיש from the beam and barrel case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה supports ריש לקיש. When the beam carrier stops and the barrel breaks, he is liable, which looks like a lying cow hurting a walking cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? It says: If the beam carrier was first and the barrel carrier was behind, and the barrel broke on the beam, he is exempt. But if the beam carrier stopped, he is liable. Here the case is like a lying cow and a walking cow, and the משנה says he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove ריש לקיש's ruling from the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam carrier who stops in the street is like the lying cow, since he is standing where he should not stay. The barrel carrier who keeps walking is like the walking cow. The משנה makes the one who stopped liable, which seems to match ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say that it supports him:
If the owner of the beam was first
and the owner of the barrel was last,
and the barrel broke on the beam, he is exempt.
But if the beam owner stopped, he is liable.
And here, it is like a lying one with a walking one,
phrases.notes: The man who stopped is the 'lying cow', and the man still walking with the barrel is the 'walking cow'.

phrases.english: and it teaches that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to back up ריש לקיש's statement from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's ruling that a lying cow is liable for harming a walking cow
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: if the beam carrier stopped, he is liable for the broken barrel.

steps.title: Not a support, but actually a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It announces that the משנה does not just fail to support ריש לקיש, it actually raises a difficulty against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so? You wanted to bring support? Not only does it not support him, it is actually a difficulty against him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 12. It is setting up its next move: showing why the משנה goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not explain anything yet. It only flips the direction: the same משנה that looked like support will be used to attack ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think so? (a rejection of what was just said)

phrases.english: And can you think so?!
You wanted to support him?
It is not enough that it does not support him,
rather it is even a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempted support from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה actually goes against ריש לקיש. The reason is explained in the next step.

steps.title: ריש לקיש needs a kick, but the משנה makes him liable without one
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש makes the lying cow's owner liable only when it kicked. That implies he would be exempt if the walking cow simply bumped into it. But in the משנה the barrel carrier bumped into the beam by himself, and the beam carrier is still liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is liable is that it kicked. So if the walking cow got hurt on its own, he would be exempt. But the משנה is a case where the damage happened on its own, and it teaches that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difficulty against ריש לקיש: a precise reading of his words does not fit the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said 'the lying cow kicked', which implies that liability needs an active kick. In the משנה, the beam carrier did nothing; the barrel carrier walked into the beam. Yet the משנה says the beam carrier is חייב, which goes against what ריש לקיש's words imply.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is only because of...
By itself, without anyone actively doing it

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the question of whether someone who stands where he should not is liable even when the other person bumps into him.

phrases.english: The reason is that it kicked;
phrases.notes: He means: ריש לקיש made the lying cow liable only because it actively kicked.

phrases.english: but if it was damaged by itself, he is exempt;
but the משנה is a case of 'by itself',
phrases.notes: The barrel carrier walked into the beam. The man who stopped did not hit him.

phrases.english: and it teaches that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the difficulty that step 13 announced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's words imply that he is exempt without a kick, but the משנה makes the beam carrier liable even when the damage happened by itself.

steps.title: The beam blocked the whole road, but the cow left room to pass
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the difficulty against ריש לקיש. In the משנה the beam blocked the entire road, so the barrel carrier had no choice. In ריש לקיש's case the cow lay on one side, so the walking cow should have gone around.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a beam that blocked the whole road, like a dead animal lying across it. Here, ריש לקיש is talking about a cow lying on one side of the road. The other cow should have walked on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by showing that the משנה and his case are not the same situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty was that the beam carrier is liable even though the barrel carrier bumped into him. The answer is that the beam left no way around it, so the barrel carrier could not avoid it. ריש לקיש's lying cow took up only one side, so a walking cow that bumps into it has itself to blame.

keyTerms.meaning: A carcass, a dead body lying across the way

phrases.english: The משנה is where it blocked the road like a carcass;
phrases.notes: "It" is the beam. It stretched across the whole road, so there was no way to get past it.

phrases.english: here, it is where it lay down on one side,
so it should have walked on the other side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by telling apart the case of the משנה and the case of ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא of the facts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The beam carrier is liable for a plain collision, so ריש לקיש should make a lying cow's owner liable for a plain collision too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beam carrier is liable only because the beam blocked the whole road. A lying cow that leaves room to pass does not make its owner liable for a collision.

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to support ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now tries a proof from the end of the משנה. If the barrel carrier is in front and stops, and the beam carrier walks into him, the beam carrier is exempt. That looks like a walking cow hurting a lying cow, where ריש לקיש also says exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the end of the משנה supports ריש לקיש. It teaches that if the barrel carrier was in front and the beam carrier behind, and the barrel broke on the beam, the beam carrier is liable. But if the barrel carrier stopped, the beam carrier is exempt. This case is like a walking cow against a lying cow, and the משנה says exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from the first part of the משנה to its last part and tries to use it as a proof for ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the roles are reversed. The barrel carrier stopped, like the lying cow, and the beam carrier kept walking, like the walking cow. The משנה exempts the walker, which matches ריש לקיש's ruling that a walking cow that kicks a lying cow is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
A cow that is lying down

phrases.english: Rather, the last part of the משנה
supports ריש לקיש,
as it teaches: If the barrel owner was first
and the beam owner was last,
and the barrel broke on the beam, he is liable.
But if the barrel owner stopped, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The one who is exempt is the beam carrier, who kept walking into the barrel carrier after he stopped.

phrases.english: And here, it is like a walking cow against a lying cow,
and it teaches that he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סֵיפָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the רישא now explained away, the גמרא looks for support for ריש לקיש in the סיפא instead.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's ruling that a walking cow that kicks a lying cow is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: when the barrel carrier in front stops, the beam carrier walking behind is exempt.

steps.title: Walking normally is not the same as kicking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the משנה the beam carrier was just walking the normal way. A kick is different: the lying cow can say, 'You may walk past me, but you may not kick me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the משנה, the beam carrier was walking in his normal way. Here, the lying cow can say to the walking cow: 'Even if you have permission to walk over me, you have no permission to kick me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 16. The סיפא does not support ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam carrier is exempt because he did nothing unusual; he was simply walking. Kicking is an extra, unusual act that the walker has no right to do. So the משנה does not prove that a walking cow that kicks is exempt, and ריש לקיש's ruling stays without support from here.
steps.whatToRemember: Bumping while walking normally is treated differently from kicking. Permission to walk by is not permission to strike.

phrases.english: In the משנה, he was walking in his normal way;
here, she can say to her:
phrases.notes: The גמרא pictures the lying cow speaking to the walking cow, as if the animals could argue their case.

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּאִית לִךְ רְשׁוּת לְסַגּוֹיֵי עֲלַי,
phrases.english: Even if you have permission to walk over me,
you have no permission to kick me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ראיה of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the סיפא is set aside.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treated normal walking as the same thing as kicking. Kicking is an extra act the walker has no right to do, so the case in the משנה may be decided differently from a kick.

steps.title: New משנה: two people walking or running who hurt each other
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If two people are in the public domain, whether both walking, one running and one walking, or both running, and they hurt each other, both are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two people were walking in the public domain, or one was running and one walking, or both were running, and they hurt each other. Both of them are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about people who collide with each other in a public place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three situations: both walking, one running and one walking, and both running. In all of them, when they hurt each other, neither one has to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, a public area

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: משנה: Two people who were walking in the public domain,
one running and one walking,
or both of them were running,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִזִּיקוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה – שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.english: and they hurt each other, both of them are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the beam-and-barrel discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people in the public domain who hurt each other, whether walking or running, are both exempt.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow איסי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה, which exempts a runner, disagrees with איסי בן יהודה. In a ברייתא he says a runner who causes damage is liable because running is unusual. He agrees the runner is exempt at בין השמשות on ערב שבת, because then running is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow איסי בן יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that he says: someone who runs is liable, because running is unusual. But איסי agrees that on ערב שבת at twilight the runner is exempt, because then he runs with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that our משנה, which exempts a runner, disagrees with a תנא named איסי בן יהודה. It quotes his view from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that even if one person was running and the other walking, they are both exempt. איסי בן יהודה says running in the street is unusual behavior, so the runner pays. He makes one exception: on ערב שבת at twilight, running counts as running with permission, so the runner is exempt. The גמרא asks why in Step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Unusual or out of the ordinary
Twilight on Friday, just before Shabbat begins
With permission, in a way that is allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that running is 'unusual' except when it has a good reason is the key to the whole discussion that follows.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּאִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: GEMARA: Our Mishnah is not like Isi ben Yehuda.
As it was taught: Isi ben Yehuda says:
One who runs is liable, because he is acting unusually.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה אִיסִי בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
phrases.english: And Isi agrees that on Friday at twilight
he is exempt, because he runs with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the משנה quoted in Step 18 and shows a תנא who disagrees with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to איסי בן יהודה, a runner who causes damage is liable, except on ערב שבת at twilight.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like Isi ben Yehuda
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה, so a runner on a regular day is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a final ruling in favor of איסי בן יהודה. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling like איסי means that, in practice, a runner who damages on a regular weekday must pay. This seems to clash with our משנה, which exempts the runner.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows the opinion of...
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The law is like Isi ben Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּאִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement presented in Step 19 in favor of איסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה: a runner is liable, except on ערב שבת at twilight.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן follows an unattributed משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. He has a rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and our unattributed משנה exempts a runner. So how can he rule like איסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? Doesn't רבי יוחנן say that the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה? And our משנה taught: if one was running and one was walking, or both were running, they are exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling by setting it against another rule of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general principle: when a משנה gives a law without naming anyone, that is the הלכה. Our משנה, without naming anyone, exempts a runner. So ruling like איסי, who makes the runner liable, seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's own principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (a challenge formula)
An unattributed משנה, stated with no name attached

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The law follows an unattributed Mishnah,
and we learned: one running and one walking,
or both were running, they are exempt!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from Step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 20 using רבי יוחנן's own principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling like איסי בן יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. Our סתם משנה exempts a runner, and that contradicts איסי.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about Friday at twilight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה is speaking about ערב שבת at בין השמשות. At that time even איסי agrees the runner is exempt, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about Friday at twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting our משנה to the one time when even איסי agrees the runner is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is only about ערב שבת at twilight, then it fits איסי's opinion. So רבי יוחנן can follow the סתם משנה and still rule like איסי for regular days.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is about Friday at twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה to a specific time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה exempts a runner at all times, which goes against איסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה exempts the runner only on ערב שבת at twilight, which איסי agrees with.

steps.title: Proof from the extra case of both running
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the משנה is about ערב שבת. It proves it from the extra case of 'both running.' If a runner is exempt even when the other was only walking, then it is obvious he is exempt when both were running, so why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From the fact that it teaches: 'or both were running, they are exempt.' Why do I need this too? Now that one running and one walking is exempt, is there any need to say that when both are running they are exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for its answer and points to a case in the משנה that seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exempting a runner who hit someone who was walking is the bigger case. Exempting him when the other person was also running is obvious. So the extra case is a hint that the משנה must be read in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches
Why do I need this as well?
Now that X is true, is it even necessary to say Y?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָתָנֵי: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם רָצִין – פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.english: From the fact that it teaches: or both were running, they are exempt.
Why do I need this too?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא אֶחָד רָץ וְאֶחָד מְהַלֵּךְ – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: Now if one running and one walking is exempt,
is it necessary to say both running?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer given in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה is talking about ערב שבת at twilight
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra, seemingly unneeded case in the משנה of 'both running'

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: Friday versus weekday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. One running and one walking is exempt only on ערב שבת at twilight, but on a weekday the runner is liable. If both were running, they are exempt even on a weekday. This explains why both cases are mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: one running and one walking is exempt. When is this said? On Friday at twilight. But on a weekday, one running and one walking, the runner is liable. If both were running, even on a weekday they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof by explaining how the משנה should be read so that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases now teach two different laws. 'One running, one walking' is exempt only before Shabbat. 'Both running' is exempt even on a weekday. Now the משנה fully matches איסי and רבי יוחנן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say
In what case is this said?

steps.whatToRemember: A runner who hurts a walker is liable on a regular day and exempt only on ערב שבת at twilight. If both were running, both are exempt even on a weekday. So רבי יוחנן rules like איסי without going against the סתם משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as 'running is always exempt.' After this rereading, the case of one running and one walking is limited to ערב שבת. Only the case of both running is exempt on a weekday too.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it says:
One running and one walking is exempt.
When is this said?
On Friday at twilight,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּחוֹל – אֶחָד רָץ וְאֶחָד מְהַלֵּךְ, חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: but on a weekday, one running and one walking, he is liable.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the one who was running.

phrases.english: Both running: even on a weekday they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof of Step 23 by rereading the משנה, and closes the challenge of Step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה exempts one running and one walking only on ערב שבת at twilight. Both running are exempt even on a weekday. This fits איסי בן יהודה and רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: What permission is there to run on Friday at twilight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that איסי agrees a runner on ערב שבת at twilight is פטור because he runs ברשות. It then asks what makes running at that time 'with permission.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: And איסי agrees that on ערב שבת at בין השמשות the runner is exempt, because he is running with permission. What kind of permission is there on ערב שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא it just used and asks for the reason behind it. It wants to know why running on Friday at twilight counts as allowed running.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer in Step 22 depended on the idea that on ערב שבת the runner is running ברשות. On a normal day running in the street is unusual, so the runner is responsible. The גמרא now asks what is special about Friday at twilight that makes running there normal and allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said". This is how the גמרא goes back to quote a line from a source it already brought.
Agrees, admits. Here איסי agrees in one special case.
Twilight, the unclear time between sunset and night
With permission. The person is doing something that is allowed and normal.

phrases.english: The Master said: And Isi agrees
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of איסי בן יהודה quoted in Step 19. Now the גמרא goes back to look at it more closely.

phrases.english: on the eve of Shabbat at twilight
that he is exempt, because he runs with permission.
On the eve of Shabbat, what permission is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the reading of the משנה, the גמרא goes back to explain the reason given in the ברייתא for the ערב שבת exception.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes running on ערב שבת at twilight count as running ברשות?

steps.title: The answer begins: like רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by pointing to something רבי חנינא used to say. The words of רבי חנינא come in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי חנינא, for רבי חנינא used to say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It tells us the reason is connected to רבי חנינא's practice, and his actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will come from how great people behaved on Friday before שבת. If a rabbi was known to say and do this, then rushing at that time is a proper, accepted thing and not careless running. That is what would make it ברשות.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose saying about ערב שבת explains the permission to run
"Like" or "in line with". The answer matches what someone else said.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the answer in this line. It only names the source. רבי חנינא's actual words come at the start of the next עמוד.

phrases.english: It is like Rabbi Chanina –
for Rabbi Chanina would say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the question of Step 25 by bringing in רבי חנינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission comes from the practice of רבי חנינא on ערב שבת. His exact words follow in the next line.
